Physical Divisions i. Natural Regions of India *Paleomagnetism is the branch that studies the magnetic properties preserved in the rocks, sediments or other such things during their formation. This branch of science is helpful in the study of ancient geological phenomena. According to continental drift theory, the Indian mainland is a part of Gondwanaland. Gondwanaland includes present day Peninsular India, Australia, Africa, Arabian Peninsula, South America and regions of Antarctica. *In the mid Mesozoic era (Jurassic Period, 144-208 Million Years Ago), Gondwanaland split into a number of pieces through convection currents. The Indian plate started drifting towards north after splitting from Gondwanaland. Consequently, the Indian plate, moving towards north, collided with a bigger plate, called the Eurasian plate. Due to this collision, the sedimentary rocks of the Tethys Sea, between the two plates (i.e., Indian and Eurasian), folded and developed into the Himalayas and mountain ranges of West Asia. The whole mountain range of the Himalayas represents a youthful topography. It has high peaks, deep valleys (gorges), and fast - flowing rivers. In the Terai region of the Himalayas, artesian wells are also found. *Due to upliftment of Tethys Sea in the Himalayas and the subsidence of the northern flank of the peninsular plateau, resulted in the formation of a large basin. With the passage of time, this basin was gradually filled with sedimentary deposits of rivers flowing from Northern mountains and Peninsular Plateau. In this way, a vast land area of alluvial deposits was developed as the ‘Northern Plain’ of India. *Geologically, Peninsular Plateau is the ancient part of Earth’s surface. *Peninsular Plateau is the most stable region of India. Peninsular Plateau comprises of hills and broad valleys which are made up of igneous and metamorphic rocks. Meghalaya plateau is an extension of Peninsular plateau. It was separated from Indian Peninsula through Malda Gap due to faulting. The Western Coast of India was formed due to faulting and subsidence of the western flank of the plateau. *The Indian mainland shows a large variation in the physical structure. Therefore India is divided into four natural regions. These are -
1. Northern Mountains
2. Northern Plains
3. Peninsular Plateau and
4. Coastal Plains & Islands. *Based on the variations in its geological structure and formations, India can be divided into 3 primary and 6 sub-physical geomorphic regions- 1. The Northern and North-Eastern Mountains. 2. The Northern Plain 3. The Indian Desert 4. The Peninsular Plateau
5. The Coastal Plain
6. The Islands Eastern Hills and Mountains Indo - Gangetic Brahmaputra Plain Highlands Map Not to Scale 1. The paleomagnetic results obtained from India indicate that in the past, the Indian land mass has moved :
y2abfc7fc2cd.x: The Indian landmass has moved northward. This is evident from the paleomagnetic results obtained from India. Even the extension of the plateau region on the north side is evident. Paleomagnetism is the study of the record of the Earth's magnetic field in rocks, sediment or archaeological materials. This record provides information on the past behavior of Earth's magnetic field and the past location of tectonic plates.
